title: Lost GET — Reporting and Recovery
body: A missing tooth or shroud that rides through the cycle unnoticed ends up in the primary crusher — that's severe liner damage, a plant stoppage, and a jammed-liner repair that's one of the ugliest safety jobs on site. It's entirely preventable, and it's expensive precisely because it's preventable.
keyPoints: Stop first, always. If GET loss is suspected or confirmed, the operator stops immediately — no "finish the pass and check after."
Report with specifics: equipment ID, operator, GPS location, and exactly what's missing. Vague reports slow the search and widen the isolation zone.
Survey pinpoints the search area, especially on ore blocks where muck moves fast through load-and-haul — the window to recover closes quickly.
If it isn't found, the loader operator at the ROM pad feeding the crusher is the last line of defense — every load gets a visual check before it's fed.
Prevention beats recovery every time: pre-start GET checks, documented change-outs (including single-tooth replacements), and operators trained to recognize the feel/sound of a lost tooth.
apply: Any loading face working broken ground after a blast — that's exactly where a tooth or adapter separates unnoticed, so a five-second GET check at bucket cycle start costs nothing next to a crusher rebuild.
